The increasing width of the confidence intervals directly reflects the escalating uncertainty associated with forecasting further into the future. For the 1-day horizon, the narrow interval of [135.06, 140.58] primarily accounts for very short-term market volatility, daily news, or minor price fluctuations. Extending to 1-week, the interval widens to [131.1, 144.9], encompassing a broader range of potential influences such as weekly economic data releases, minor policy announcements, or developing sentiment shifts. For the 1-month forecast, the significantly wider range of [124.65, 152.35] acknowledges the substantial uncertainty introduced by potential macroeconomic changes, more significant policy decisions, earnings reports (if applicable to the forecast item), and other unforeseen events that have more time to materialize and impact the value. Essentially, the longer the time horizon, the more variables can come into play, making precise prediction less certain.

While my confidence intervals encompass a reasonably broad range of expected outcomes, certain extreme and unforeseen events could push the actual results beyond these boundaries. On the upside, an unexpected major positive catalyst, such as a significant technological breakthrough, a substantial and unforeseen boost in demand, or a highly favorable economic stimulus package, could drive the value above 152.35. Conversely, severe negative shocks could push the outcome below 124.65. Examples include a sudden and sharp economic recession, a major geopolitical crisis, a significant regulatory change that negatively impacts the underlying asset or market, or a "black swan" event with widespread disruptive effects. These are typically high-impact, low-probability events that lie outside the scope of typical market fluctuations captured by the standard intervals.
